newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-PADRES OUTSCORE ROCKIES AS GWYNN, WALKER GO OVER .400.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-PADRES OUTSCORE ROCKIES AS GWYNN, WALKER GO OVER .400.

text.p: Steve Finley smacked a two-run homer and Tony Gwynn went 3-for-5 to extend his hitting streak to 17 games and raise his batting average over .400 as the San Diego Padres outscored the Colorado Rockies 11-7 Saturday.

Finley hit his 17th homer in the first off starter Bill Swift (4-2). The Padres added two more in the inning and scored twice in both the third and fourth. They tacked on three runs in the fifth to build an 11-0 cushion.
"At Coors Field you never think you have enough," said Padres manager Bruce Bochy.
Gwynn had a single in the first, an RBI double in the fourth and a run-scoring single in the fifth, raising his average from .399 to .402. He has hit safely in 40 of his last 42 games.

Colorado's Larry Walker went 3-for-5 and also is hitting .402. "It's frustrating when a team is in last place or near last place and you go up there and have days like Tony and I did," Walker said. "You boost your averages over .400 and you come back and say 'who cares?'"
The Padres are in fourth and last place in the National League West while Colorado is 3-1/2 games ahead of them in third, 8-1/2 behind first-place San Francisco.
Joey Hamilton (7-3) got the victory, his third straight, despite allowing seven runs and 13 hits in 6 1/3 innings.
Jim Bruske and Trevor Hoffman held the Rockies scoreless over the final 2 2/3 innings to preserve the victory. Colorado has dropped eight of its last nine games.
Swift was tagged for six runs and eight hits in just three innings. Mike DeJean came on in the fourth and wasn't any better, surrendering five runs and five hits in 1 1/3 innings.

In Los Angeles, Mark Lewis and Rick Wilkins hit back-to-back homers with one out in the top of the ninth to ignite a seven-run outburst as the San Francisco Giants stunned the Dodgers 8-5, ending their eight-game win streak.

Jeff Kent capped the inning with a two-run homer, giving him 20 homers and 68 RBI, surpassing Robby Thompson for the San Francisco record by a second baseman in both categories. Rogers Hornsby holds the franchise mark in both.
Julian Tavarez (3-2) worked a scoreless eighth to get the win for the Giants. Todd Worrell (1-2) took the loss.
Mike Piazza and Todd Hollandsworth homered for the Dodgers, who lost for the first time in July.
Worrell surrendered six runs -- three earned -- and five hits while retiring only one batter.

In Atlanta, Greg Maddux overcame a rough start for his fifth straight win and Ryan Klesko belted a three-run homer as the Braves snapped a three-game losing streak with a 7-4 victory that cooled off the New York Mets.

Maddux (12-3), who started the All-Star Game for the National League on Tuesday, allowed three runs in the first two innings but settled down, retiring 12 in a row until Carlos Baerga doubled with two out in the sixth.
Despite allowing a walk for the first time in six starts, Maddux joined a four-way tie for the N.L. lead in wins. He allowed six hits in seven innings, walking two and striking out eight.
Mark Wohlers got the final three outs for his 21st save in 23 opportunities.
Mark Clark (7-6) took the loss.
In Chicago, pinch-hitter Danny Sheaffer's single with one out in the top of the 12th scored Tom Lampkin from second and lifted the St Louis Cardinals to a 2-1 victory over the Cubs.

Turk Wendell (2-5), who pitched a scoreless 11th, retired the first batter of the 12th. But Lampkin singled to right, John Mabry singled to left and Sheaffer, batting for reliever T.J. Mathews, laced a single to centre for the go-ahead run.
Mathews (4-3) allowed a hit over two scoreless innings in relief of Andy Benes, who matched a season high with 12 strikeouts over nine innings. Dennis Eckersley worked the 12th for his 20th save.
In Cincinnati, Eduardo Perez smacked a three-run homer and Mike Kelly snapped a fifth-inning tie with a solo shot as the Red edged the Montreal Expos 4-3, halting a three-game losing streak.

John Smiley (7-10) allowed three runs and six hits over seven innings for his second straight win after losing four in a row. Stan Belinda pitched the eighth and Jeff Shaw struck out two in the ninth for his 19th save in 21 opportunities.

At Florida, the long-awaited pitching matchup between brothers Mark and Al Leiter was cancelled when the game between the Philadelphia Phillies and Marlins was postponed due to rain. The game will be made up in a doubleheader September 17.
